subject: SAC-B6g caller-owned workload-level residual policy envelope
intent: Evaluate an explicit caller-owned workload-class to static residual-policy mapping without inferring classes from per-item cardinality, content, margin, or semantic importance.

envelope.resolutionBoundary: Resolve accepts only an exact caller-owned workload class string. It has no Item, feature-count, margin, or cardinality input.
failClosed: empty envelope id or provenance ref

gridEvaluation.callerDeclaration: Cells with structuredPerSubchannel 1/2/4 are explicitly declared 'general'; cells with 8 are explicitly declared 'structure-preserving'. This declaration is fixture metadata, not resolver inference.

negativeControl.observation: Caller ownership and provenance do not make the declaration correct; a wrong workload class can materially worsen the synthetic margin.

findings: An exact caller-owned two-class envelope reduces mean regret on the B6f grid relative to any single fixed policy, while retaining non-zero regret and therefore remaining distinct from a cell-best oracle.
The envelope resolver requires no item content or cardinality and therefore does not convert runtime feature counts into semantic priority.
Unknown workload classes fail closed instead of silently falling back to a guessed policy.
Three narrow-structure cells still prefer cap64 while the 'general' class is fixed to cap128, preserving explicit residual regret rather than overfitting the mapping to every grid cell.
A caller misdeclaration on the t55/s8 negative control produces regret about 0.208, so caller-owned provenance improves auditability but not correctness.
stopLines: synthetic grid fit != real workload generalization

verification.independentArithmetic: B6f checked-in margins were independently aggregated for envelope regret and negative-control regret.
